messages:
lisa_account: Peregrine Health (customer) just pinged our support channel — they see sustained 500+ms tail latency and a spike of 5xx on their dedicated pool phoenix-dedicated-1. Live payments path. Customer reports timeouts on confirm endpoint. I need oncall, paging now.

incident-bot: paged @raj_oncall, severity: P0, route: customer-impact, svc: dedicated-pool, pool: phoenix-dedicated-1

raj_oncall: on it. grabbing logs, pinging SRE. can someone put customer in status page or send heartbeat msg? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

emma_ops: adding a short note to customer: "We're investigating increased latency and 5xx on your dedicated pool. Engineers are on it; we'll update shortly." — sent to Peregrine contact.

raj_oncall: quick check — control plane shows pool reporting high GPU mem usage and one host OOMing, autoscaler tried to replace but hit quota. errors look like: `kv cache miss -> NPE` in runtime logs. pulling runtime logs now.

jordan_dev: I see repeated `cuda memory alloc failed` on node gpu-az3-07, and the runtime restarted the worker process a few times. stack snippet:```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory
  at infer_loop (/app/runtime/serve.py:482)
  at handle_request (/app/runtime/serve.py:210)
```

samir_sre: joining handoff. raj — status? Do we have a temporary mitigation?

raj_oncall: spinning up a hot fallback on general-dedicated-backup pool and routing traffic for Peregrine to it (low-risk smaller model). kicking `rpool route-update --customer Peregrine --src phoenix-dedicated-1 --dst general-dedicated-backup --weight 100`

deploy-bot: route update job queued (job id: 987654). will report success/fail.

raj_oncall: route update succeeded. Traffic switched to backup pool. Early metrics — error rate down to normal, latency back to baseline for new requests. Old inflight requests still finishing/timeout, estimating recovery in ~2m.

lisa_account: Customer notified of failover and that we switched them to a backup pool. They asked if this was a scheduled maintenance — they said no and are upset about payment flow. requesting ETA to restore original pool and whether we'll issue credits.

samir_sre: root cause looks like a memory leak in the runtime library for that model variant (observed in process memory growth over hours). When the leak hit, the worker OOM'd and caused repeated restarts which saturated autoscaler and exhausted quota, preventing healthy replacement.

raj_oncall: mitigation steps done: 1) route traffic away (done). 2) scaled backup pool to handle load (done). 3) quarantined node gpu-az3-07 and removed from rotation (`rnode drain gpu-az3-07 --force`). 4) opened quota request with infra but we can't wait on that — need longer-term fix.

emma_ops: confirmed backup has been accepting 100% of traffic, customer confirmed payments are flowing again. marking customer impact resolved in status page. :white_check_mark:

lisa_account: customer wants a post-incident writeup and proposed credits. Also asking for timeline to get them back on their original pool — they want root cause + steps to avoid recurrence.

samir_sre: immediate plan: patch runtime to fix leak in model hotstart path (PR in progress), post-deploy we will warm a new set of workers and do a controlled failback. Proposed timeline: patch + canary deploy in 6 hours, full rollout in 24 hours assuming no regression.

jordan_dev: PR: https://git.internal/runtime/merge/4223 (fixes mem leak in hotstart). Tests pass locally, running integration job now.

raj_oncall: proposed customer communication draft (short):
"Hi Peregrine team — we routed your traffic to a backup pool to restore service after repeated worker restarts on phoenix-dedicated-1. Root cause: memory leak in runtime during model hotstart causing OOM and worker restarts. Mitigation: traffic routed to backup, affected node quarantined, patch in progress. Next steps: patch rollout and controlled failback; ETA ~24 hours. We propose a service credit equivalent to 10% of last billing period for the period your traffic was on backup + 5% goodwill credit. We'll follow up with a full RCA."

lisa_account: 👍 can we soften numbers slightly? customer is sensitive. Also need exec summary for Peregrine CISO and our AE.

samir_sre: Exec summary (one-liner):
"Service disruption for Peregrine payments due to a memory leak in the inference runtime causing worker OOM and cascading autoscaler exhaustion; immediate failover to backup pool restored service; patch and controlled failback planned."

raj_oncall: assigning follow-ups: @jordan_dev to finish PR and coordinate canary; @samir_sre to own RCA draft; @lisa_account to own customer comms and credit negotiation; @emma_ops to confirm status page + billing ticket.

jordan_dev: will finish canary by EOD and monitor. will post logs and a canary dashboard link here.

samir_sre: starting RCA draft now — I'll include timeline, logs (OOM traces), memory growth graphs, autoscaler behavior, and remediation: runtime patch + autoscaler safeguards (limit rapid replacement, add mem-growth alert), and recommend a dedicated quota buffer for paid dedicated pools.

lisa_account: for credits, proposing: 7% credit for duration (2hr incident window) + 3% goodwill = 10% total. we can flex based on AE negotiation. please flag if legal needs to review.

emma_ops: billing ticket created #BILL-4521 with proposed credit 10%. tagging finance and billing.

incident-bot: incident severity downgraded to P2 after service restored for customer and no additional errors observed for 15m.

raj_oncall: handing off to samir for RCA and to lisa for comms. I'll remain on watch for another hour then stand down. paging next oncall if regression.

samir_sre: noted. will post RCAdraft in this thread before EOD for review. will include proposed SLA verbiage to avoid repeated surprises (eg, dedicated pool buffer + alerting).

lisa_account: thanks team. Peregrine AE looped in (cc: @Peregrine-AE). I'll send the softer customer note now and schedule a follow-up call tomorrow with their ops/CISO.

jordan_dev: can everyone review the PR when CI finishes — want to avoid a quick rollback. linking canary logs once available.

lisa_account: final note for thread — customer asked if action items will be included in contractual SLA update. we should prepare a short doc for AE/legal outlining recommended SLA changes (dedicated quota guard, priority patching window).

samir_sre: added SLA actionables to RCA TODO. leaving this thread open until RCA posted.

emma_ops: status page updated, billing updated, customer notified, can close paging.

raj_oncall: standing down now. :hand:

samir_sre: (later) RCA draft posted: https://docs.internal/incidents/2401234567-rca-draft — folks pls review.

lisa_account: acknowledged. will incorporate feedback and send to customer + execs after internal review.

(REACTIONS: many :thumbsup: on the failover messages, :eyes: on the RCA draft link)
